case.subject: AI-assisted accessibility for live performance
case.tool: OpenAI Whisper (integrated via independent accessibility tool)
case.problem: Deaf or hard-of-hearing audience members missing nuances in unscripted, improvised theater or live community events where closed captioning is not pre-written.
case.workflow: A theater technician uses a laptop running Whisper-based transcription to ingest live audio from the stage. The agent processes the audio in near real-time, displaying generated captions on a screen visible to the audience. Human oversight involves a technician monitoring for major errors and toggling the system on/off during intermission or set changes.
case.result: Improved audience inclusion by providing live, automated accessibility for unscripted dialogue, allowing deaf attendees to follow comedic timing and improvised audience interactions.
case.result_basis: Independent reporting and community accessibility project documentation.
case.measurement_context: Qualitative improvement in accessibility as reported by venue attendees and local accessibility advocates; no quantitative accuracy percentage claimed.
case.source_quote: Automated captioning tools have begun to bridge the gap for unscripted performances where pre-recorded subtitles are impossible to provide.
case.limitation: The tool can struggle with overlapping dialogue or heavy accents; requires a stable microphone setup and a person to manage the display interface.
case.listener_action: For your next small local event, test a whisper-based transcription tool by recording a 5-minute conversation with background noise to see if it captures names and specific terminology correctly before relying on it for live accessibility.
case.availability: Available via various open-source wrappers of the OpenAI Whisper API.

case.subject: In-house theatre surtitling
case.problem: Performing arts venues frequently struggle with the high cost and logistical complexity of outsourcing professional surtitling and captioning services for live theatre and opera.
case.workflow: Venues import their production scripts into the platform; the AI detects and splits dialogue into readable surtitle chunks, which staff then style and manage in the cloud for display on venue screens or audience devices.
case.result: The tool enables theatres to produce professional-grade surtitles in-house, significantly lowering costs and making live captioning feasible for a wider range of productions.
case.result_basis: Independent product review and platform documentation.
case.measurement_context: Reported usage by over 600 theatres and festivals for in-house caption management.
case.source_quote: Captitles' lane is the room: turning a script into accurate, well-timed, well-styled captions that open a performance to deaf and hard-of-hearing patrons
case.limitation: Real-time automatic cueing remains on the roadmap; AI translation still requires human verification, and the system provides text, not sign language.
case.listener_action: Check your local theatre's accessibility page to see if they offer captioning, then ask if they handle surtitling in-house or outsource it.
case.availability: Generally available; web-based application for theatre professionals.
